title: Export fine-tuned models to GGUF and deploy on Ollama
description: Export a fine-tuned model to GGUF and deploy to Ollama with Soup CLI in three commands. Quantization levels and one-liner pipeline.

headings.title: 0. Build llama.cpp first, if you want a quantized GGUF
Running the llama.cpp programs with soup llama

blocks.html:
Export fine-tuned models to GGUF and deploy on Ollama

After training with Soup CLI, export your model to GGUF format and serve it locally with Ollama in three commands.

0. Build llama.cpp first, if you want a quantized GGUF

Soup auto-clones llama.cpp (pinned at tag b5270) into ~/.soup/llama.cpp on first use, but it does not build it. Converting to f16 or f32 works from the Python script alone. Every quantized type additionally needs the llama-quantize binary, so build it once:

blocks.code:
cd ~/.soup/llama.cpp
cmake -B build -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --config Release --target llama-quantize -j 4

blocks.html:
Soup finds the binary in both the single-config layout (build/bin/llama-quantize, from Make or Ninja) and the multi-config one (build/bin/Release/llama-quantize.exe, from MSVC or Xcode), or on your PATH. To use a checkout you already have, pass --llama-cpp /path/to/llama.cpp or set LLAMA_CPP_PATH.

On Windows the validated toolchain is Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools with the "Desktop development with C++" workload plus CMake 3.14 or newer, CPU-only. Linux and macOS need only a C++ toolchain and CMake. CUDA builds of llama.cpp are untested.

Do not run pip install -r ~/.soup/llama.cpp/requirements.txt. It pins torch~=2.2.1 against the CPU wheel index, so it will downgrade a CUDA PyTorch and break training. Soup deliberately installs only the convert script's own extras (gguf, sentencepiece, protobuf), unpinned.

Two checks before the toolchain work (v0.77.0). A model whose architecture the pinned b5270 converter cannot convert, Qwen3.5 among them, is refused before anything is cloned or installed, with Select a compatible checkout with --llama-cpp <dir>. (exit 1); moving the pin is open upstream (#1911). A newer checkout passed with --llama-cpp must also advertise --no-mtp for a merged model that declares MTP layers but saved no MTP tensors, which Soup then converts with that flag. And in an environment that manages its own packages, --no-install-deps makes Soup check gguf, sentencepiece and protobuf and refuse, naming the missing ones, instead of running pip. It does not stop the clone, so pair it with --llama-cpp or LLAMA_CPP_PATH. --verbose streams the converter's and quantizer's output as it runs. Both flags are for --format gguf only; see Model Export.

1. Export to GGUF

Quantization levels:

QuantSize (7B)QualityUse case
q4_k_m~4.1 GBGoodDefault — best size/quality balance
q5_k_m~4.8 GBBetterWhen you need higher accuracy
q8_0~7.5 GBNear-losslessBenchmarks, eval
q4_0~3.8 GBLowerThe smallest rung --quant accepts
f16 / f32~14 GB / ~28 GBUnquantizedA conversion with no quantization step

--quant accepts exactly these six values (q4_0, q4_k_m, q5_k_m, q8_0, f16, f32) and exits 1 on anything else, so the smaller llama.cpp rungs like q2_k and q3_k_m are not reachable through Soup.

2. Deploy to Ollama

Soup CLI ships with Ollama integration (v0.18.0+):

This creates an Ollama Modelfile, imports the GGUF, and registers your model.

3. Chat

blocks.code:
soup train --config soup.yaml && \
soup export --model ./output --format gguf --quant q4_k_m --output ./my-model.gguf && \
soup deploy ollama --model ./my-model.gguf --name my-model --yes

blocks.html:
soup train writes to the config's output: directory (./output unless you set it), and there is no latest subdirectory, so point --model at that directory. Without --output, soup export names the file <model-name>.<quant>.gguf and writes it next to the model directory (./output.q4_k_m.gguf), not inside it, so pass --output when a later command has to find the file. --yes skips the confirmation prompt of soup deploy ollama. In a script or CI job, pass --yes to soup train as well: since v0.77.0, with stdin piped or redirected and no --yes, it exits 3 instead of waiting for a confirmation nobody can give.

Running the llama.cpp programs with soup llama

soup llama <subcommand> [args...] starts one of five llama.cpp programs and forwards your arguments to it unchanged:

Soup commandProgram it starts
soup llama clillama-cli
soup llama mtmd-clillama-mtmd-cli
soup llama gguf-splitllama-gguf-split
soup llama serverllama-server
soup llama quantizellama-quantize

blocks.code:
soup llama quantize ./my-model.f16.gguf ./my-model.Q5_K_M.gguf Q5_K_M
soup llama server -m ./my-model.gguf --port 8080

blocks.html:
The arguments are llama.cpp's own syntax, not Soup's, and they depend on the llama.cpp build you installed. A few things are Soup's:

  • The program must be on your PATH. It is looked up by name only. Setting LLAMA_CPP_HOME does not make Soup find it, and neither does the ~/.soup/llama.cpp/build/bin directory from step 0 above: soup export searches that directory itself, soup llama does not, so add it to PATH first.
  • When the program is missing the command prints llama-quantize not found on PATH; install llama.cpp or set LLAMA_CPP_HOME (with the name of the program you asked for) and exits 2.
  • --help after the subcommand shows Soup's help, not the program's. Run the program itself for its own options.
  • Arguments are limited: at most 64, each at most 1024 characters, with no NUL or line break in any of them. Otherwise it exits 2 before starting anything.
  • The program runs with a reduced environment. HF_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY and every other variable outside a short allowlist are dropped (the list is in the CLI reference). Its output goes straight to your terminal and its exit code becomes the exit code of soup llama.

Other export formats

Soup CLI also supports:

  • ONNX — --format onnx for cross-platform inference
  • TensorRT-LLM — --format tensorrt for NVIDIA optimized serving
  • Hugging Face — not an export format. A merged checkpoint comes from soup merge --adapter <path> --output <dir>. The formats soup export accepts are gguf, gguf-ud, onnx, tensorrt, bitnet, tq1_0 and torchao; AWQ and GPTQ export were removed in v0.77.0, and they need v0.76.x and its [awq] or [gptq] extra, for example pip install "soup-cli[awq]<0.77"; upstream notes that both projects are archived and incompatible with [train] (see Model Export). Only the GGUF family (gguf, gguf-ud, bitnet, tq1_0) can be passed to --deploy ollama; the other formats are refused before the export starts, because Ollama cannot load them.
